name: Held Item Change
desc: Player changes their selected hotbar slot.

writeup.p: C09 carries one int: the hotbar slot index the client is switching to. The server's processHeldItemChange validates 0 <= slot < 9 and sets the player's currentItem, which changes the server-side held item used for reach, damage, block breaking and what other players see. It is the cheapest stateful packet in the play state: no position, no timestamp, so clients can spam it freely, which is exactly why silent-switch modules rely on it.

NetHandlerPlayServer.processHeldItemChange: if the slot is within the hotbar, set inventory.currentItem and mark the player active; otherwise log a warning. The client-side vanilla path is EntityPlayerSP/PlayerControllerMP updating the slot when the user scrolls. Because the server trusts the packet entirely, any module that sends C09 with a different slot than the visible one desynchronizes the server's view of the held item.

Three families across the 8 clients. (1) Silent switching: Scaffold (Tenacity ScaffoldModule, Rise 5.99 Scaffold, Sigma Scaffold) sends C09 to the block slot while the visible hotbar stays put, and cancels incoming C09 echoes. (2) Tool/weapon automation: Rise 6.2.4 NewNewBreaker switches to the best tool before breaking, KillAura (Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30) swaps weapons for 1.9+ style switching. (3) Consumable routing: AutoPotion/AutoSoup/AutoGap/AutoHead/AutoEat (Memeware, Rise 5.99, Sigma) switch to the food/potion slot, use the item, then switch back.

The packet is unthrottled, so modules can switch slots 20 times per tick. The detectability comes from the server comparing the packet slot to the client's own S09PacketHeldItemChange echoes and to attack/place packets: an aura that attacks with a sword while C09 says a block is held gets flagged by rotation+slot correlation checks. Silent switch modules therefore cancel the visible slot change or re-send it after the action.

implementation.overview: The slot-switch packet that silent everything depends on. Scaffold switches to blocks invisibly, breakers grab the best tool, and consumable modules hop to the potion slot and back. The server trusts the int, so the entire game is keeping the visible slot in sync with the action slot.
implementation.server_handling: processHeldItemChange validates the slot range and sets inventory.currentItem. There is no rate limit and no validation against the client's last known slot. The side effect is that the server-side held item drives entity equipment broadcasts (S04PacketEntityEquipment) and the player's attack/place behavior.
implementation.protocol_notes: Single VarInt slot field. Sent in PLAY state only. Vanilla sends it on scroll wheel input; modules send it via PacketUtil.sendPacket, addToSendQueue, or addToSendQueueNoEvent (Tenacity). Silent-switch modules cancel the packet when it matches the player's real current slot so the visible hotbar never moves.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats correlate C09 with C02/C08/C07: switching to a sword then attacking with reach is normal, but attacking while the C09 stream says a block is held trips slot-consistency checks on Verus and newer NCP. The fix in clients is to send C09 to the weapon slot before the attack and back after, or to cancel the switch entirely and spoof the attack slot.

modules.name: Scaffold (silent switch)
modules.purpose: Switch the server-side held item to the block slot without moving the visible hotbar.
modules.how_it_works: Tenacity ScaffoldModule sends C09 to the target slot via addToSendQueueNoEvent (line ~80), cancels incoming C09 packets that would reveal the switch (line ~150), and restores the original slot with a second C09 (line ~183). Rise 5.99 Scaffold sends C09 only when the computed block slot differs from the player's current slot, and cancels all C09 on the send event.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent for placement + switch; PacketSendEvent to cancel C09 echoes.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The visible-hotbar cancellation makes the server see a different slot than spectators; servers that mirror S09 back detect the mismatch. Block placement with a silently-switched slot is otherwise indistinguishable from a scroll.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Scaffold.java sends C09 through PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent and cancels all C09 in onPacketSend; Sigma 4.11 Scaffold.java includes its own switch logic. Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 Scaffold do not construct C09 directly (Slot component + custom packets).

modules.name: NewNewBreaker (AutoTool)
modules.purpose: Break blocks (including through walls) while automatically switching to the best tool via C09.
modules.how_it_works: Finds the target block with a raycast or surroundings scan, computes the best tool slot with SlotUtil, sends C09 to that slot, digs with C07, then switches back to the original slot. On attack events it also swaps to the weapon slot. The breaker mode determines target selection (Through Walls / Surroundings).
modules.vanilla_hook: PreUpdateEvent for digging; AttackEvent for weapon switch; PacketUtil.send for C09.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Rapid tool switching followed by instant block break is the classic nuker signature; Watchdog checks break speed vs tool tier. The module is primarily aimed at bed/obsidian breaking on HCF servers where fast break is expected.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 ships the same module. KillAura in Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 also sends C09 pairs (lines ~897-921, ~1018-1019) for weapon switching during attacks.

modules.name: AutoSoup / AutoPot (slot routing)
modules.purpose: Switch to the soup/potion slot, consume, and return to the combat slot, all with C09.
modules.how_it_works: On low health, find a soup/potion in the hotbar or inventory, send C09 to that slot, send the C08 use packet, then send C09 back to the original slot. Memeware AutoSoup also sends C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM and calls stopUsingItem to end the eat state cleanly so the server does not keep the player stuck eating.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Soup servers expect rapid eating, so the switch-eat-switch pattern is usually under the radar there; on vanilla combat servers the instant eat is flagged by consumption-timer checks.
modules.variations: Memeware AutoPotion mirrors it for splash potions; Rise 5.99 AutoPot/AutoSoup/AutoGap/AutoHead send C09 via PacketUtil; Sigma AutoPot/AutoSoup/AutoGApple/AutoEat do the same on their event bus.

implementation.general_hooks: MotionEvent/UpdateEvent for the switch decision; PacketSendEvent in silent-switch modules to cancel C09 echoes; sendQueue/PacketUtil for the actual send.
implementation.client_variations: Tenacity uses addToSendQueueNoEvent to bypass its own event bus. Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent. Memeware/Sigma push raw packets to the send queue. Rise 6.x routes through PacketUtil.send and the Slot component, and its PingSpoofComponent parks C09 in the blink packet class list.

anticheat.overview: The held item change packet reports the new hotbar slot. It is a thin packet, but it is the trigger for autotool, fastswitch and slot desync checks. Autotool modules switch to the best tool right before a block break or attack, so the switch timing relative to dig and use-entity packets is the signal. The slot value itself must be in range 0 to 8, and the change must match the server's view of the player's inventory, which makes out-of-range and repeated-identical-slot checks cheap and effective.

checks.name: Fastswitch (Photon)
checks.purpose: Flags hotbar switches that are faster than humanly possible while the player is in combat or using an item.
checks.how_it_works: Listens to PlayerItemHeldEvent. It first allows scroll-like changes, adjacent slots or a 0 to 8 wrap, so fast scrolling is not flagged. If the switch is non-adjacent, TPS is at least 19, ping is below the max (default 400), the last switch happened within 50 ms, and the player did something combat- or item-related in the last 750 ms, it flags with +25 VL and cancels the event at 50 VL, otherwise syncing the inventory. Violation decays 25 per 120 seconds.
checks.detects: Fastswitch and autotool modules that swap to a tool and act within the same tick.
checks.variations: Intave ToolSwitchHeuristic flags slot changes within one tick of a block break; Kauri SlotChange flags repeated identical slot packets; BetterAnticheat ImpossibleSlotCheck only checks the slot range.

checks.name: SlotChange (Kauri)
checks.purpose: Flags client-held slot changes that repeat the same slot without a server-side slot change in between.
checks.how_it_works: Two WActions: one on WrapperPlayClientHeldItemChange, one on WrapperPlayServerHeldItemChange. When the server sends a slot change, didServerSlot is set and the next client change is accepted as the echo. Otherwise a client change that equals the last slot increments a buffer that flags at 6 and decays by 3 on a legitimate change. This catches clients that spam the held-item packet to desync the server's hand tracking.
checks.detects: Slot desync abuse and clients that replay held-item packets to confuse inventory tracking.
checks.variations: Grim BadPacketsY and BetterAnticheat ImpossibleSlotCheck only validate the range; Photon Fastswitch and Intave ToolSwitchHeuristic look at timing instead.

checks.name: ImpossibleSlotCheck (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Fails any held item change whose slot is outside the hotbar range 0 to 8.
checks.how_it_works: handleReceivePlayPacket matches HELD_ITEM_CHANGE, decodes WrapperPlayClientHeldItemChange and fails when the slot is below 0 or above 8. The comment notes those values are physically impossible to send from the vanilla client.
checks.detects: Out-of-range slot packets from modified clients or crash attempts.
checks.variations: Grim BadPacketsY is the same range check with packet cancellation; Kauri SlotChange and Photon Fastswitch check repetition and timing.

checks.name: BadPacketsY (Grim)
checks.purpose: Cancels held item change packets carrying out-of-bounds slot ids before they reach the server.
checks.how_it_works: PreViaPacketReceiveListener on HELD_ITEM_CHANGE: decodes the slot and, if it is greater than 8 or below 0, flags with the slot in the verbose data, cancels the packet and calls onPacketCancel so the inventory state stays coherent.
checks.detects: Out-of-range slot ids from modified clients and crash attempts.
checks.variations: BetterAnticheat ImpossibleSlotCheck flags the same condition; Kauri SlotChange targets repeated in-range slots instead.

checks.name: ToolSwitchHeuristic (Intave)
checks.purpose: Flags slot changes made within one tick of starting and stopping a block break, the autotool signature.
checks.how_it_works: ClassicHeuristic subscribed to movement packets, which tick counters, BLOCK_DIG for break start and stop, and HELD_ITEM_SLOT_IN. If a slot change arrives within one tick after START_DESTROY_BLOCK and the player stops digging within one tick, the heuristic marks it suspicious and, when the switched slot equals the last one, accumulates a violation that flags at 4. Repeated offenses apply the DMG_LIGHT attack nerf.
checks.detects: Autotool modules that swap to the correct tool exactly when breaking starts.
checks.variations: Photon Fastswitch detects the switch speed near combat actions; Kauri SlotChange detects desync spam; Grim tracks slot changes in CompensatedInventory for its break speed checks.
